'''''Cistus salviifolius''''', common names '''sage-leaved rock-rose''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|access-date=17 October 2014|df=dmy-all}}</ref> '''salvia cistus'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=CISA|taxon=Cistus salviifolius|accessdate=17 January 2016}}</ref> or '''Gallipoli rose''', is a [[shrub]] of the family [[Cistaceae]].

==Etymology==
The genus name ''[[Cistus]]'' derives from the [[Ancient Greek]] words {{Lang|grc|κίσθος}} ({{Lang|grc-Latn|kisthos}}) meaning basket, while the species name ''salviifolius'' refers the wrinkled leaves similar to those of the sage.<ref name=ap>{{Cite web |url=http://www.actaplantarum.org/floraitaliae/viewtopic.php?t=7226 |title=Acta Plantarum |access-date=2011-09-06 |archive-date=2013-04-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130425145143/http://www.actaplantarum.org/floraitaliae/viewtopic.php?t=7226 }}</ref>

==Description==
''Cistus salviifolius'' has spreading stems covered by clumpy hairs. This bushy shrub reaches on average {{convert|30|-|60|cm}} in height, with a maximum of {{convert|100|cm}}. The oval-shaped green leaves are {{convert|1-4|cm||1|abbr=on}} long, opposite, reticulate, tomentose on both sides, with a short [[petiole (botany)|petiole]] (2–4 mm).<ref name=Pignatti>Pignatti S. - Flora d'Italia – Edagricole – 1982. Vol. II, pag. 122.</ref>

The [[inflorescence]] holds one or more round flowers, long-stalked, arranged at the leaf axils. The five white petals have a yellow spot at the base, forming a corolla {{convert|4-6|cm||1|abbr=on}} in diameter. The [[stamen]]s are also yellow and the anthers shed abundant yellow pollen. This plant is pollinated by insects ([[entomophily]]), especially by [[bee]]s. The flowering period extends from April through May. The fruit is a pentagonal capsule, 5–7 mm long.<ref name=Pignatti/>

==Phylogeny==
''Cistus salviifolius'' belongs to the white and whitish pink flowered clade of ''Cistus'' species.

==Cultivation==
''Cistus salviifolius'' cultivated in the nursery industry, and grown in gardens and public landscapes, often for its [[xeric|drought-tolerant]] and pollinator habitat attributes.

==Distribution==
This showy wildflower is native to the [[Mediterranean]] region, in southern Europe<ref name=Pignatti/> and parts of [[Western Asia]] and [[North Africa]].

==Habitat==
This plant prefers dry hills, [[scrubland]] and open woodlands, at an altitude of {{convert|0|-|1200|m}} above sea level.<ref name=Pignatti/> It regrows very quickly following a fire.

==Chemistry==
''Cistus salviifolius'' contains [[flavan-3ol]]s, [[oligomeric proanthocyanidin]]s<ref>Antioxidant oligomeric proanthocyanidins from Cistus salvifolius. Fadi Qa'dan, Frank Petereit, Kenza Mansoor and  Adolf Nahrstedt, Natural Product Research, Volume 20, Issue 13, 2006, pages 1216-1224, {{doi|10.1080/14786410600899225}}</ref> and [[prodelphinidin]]s such as [[epigallocatechin-3-O-(4-hydroxybenzoate)]], [[epigallocatechin-(4β→8)-epigallocatechin]], [[epigallocatechin -3-O-gallate-(4β→8)-epigallocatechin]], [[epigallocatechin-(4β→6)-epigallocatechin-3-O-gallate]], [[1-O-β-d -(6′-O-galloyl)-glucopyranosyl-3-methoxy-5-hydroxybenzene]], [[epigallocatechin-(4β→8)-epigallocatechin-3-O-gallate]], [[1-O-β-d- glucopyranosyl-3-methoxy-5-hydroxybenzene]] and [[rhododendrin]] (betuloside).<ref>Flavan-3-ols, prodelphinidins and further polyphenols from Cistus salvifolius. Andreas Danne, Frank Petereit and Adolf Nahrstedt, Phytochemistry, '''37''', (2), 1994, Pages 533–538, {{doi|10.1016/0031-9422(94)85094-1}}</ref> It also contains ellagitannins of the [[punicalagins|punicalagin]] type.<ref>Simultaneous LC-DAD and LC-MS Determination of Ellagitannins, Flavonoid Glycosides, and Acyl-Glycosyl Flavonoids in Cistus salvifolius L. Leaves. E. Saracini, M. Tattini, M. L. Traversi, F. F. Vincieri and P. Pinelli, Chromatographia, Volume 62, Numbers 5-6, pages 245-249, {{doi|10.1365/s10337-005-0623-7}}</ref>
